item.title: SC expands ambit of Sec 498A to cover cruelty in live-ins too
item.description: The Supreme Court has extended legal protection to live-in relationships. These relationships are now covered under Section 498A of the IPC. The court stated that the law must adapt to changing societal norms. Cruelty within such relationships will now be punishable by law. This decision aims to protect women from domestic violence and harassment.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: Census phase 2 to begin Aug 17, will capture caste, parents’ birth details
item.description: The Census 2027 population enumeration phase begins August 17 in snow-bound northern areas. This phase will capture caste details for the first time since 1931. Parents' date and birthplace will also be recorded as declared by respondents. Passport and Aadhaar numbers may be collected voluntarily during the exercise. The questionnaire for this significant census phase will be notified soon.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN

item.title: India crosses 20k organ transplants/yr for 1st time
item.description: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, a significant increase over previous years. Delhi-NCR led the nation in transplant procedures, while Tamil Nadu topped deceased organ donors. India now ranks third globally in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Deceased donor transplants continue to fall short of the substantial demand for organs. Government initiatives aim to strengthen organ donation and transplant services across the country.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: World’s largest camera captures over 500,000 galaxies in one photo of universe
item.description: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has released a stunning image of the COSMOS field. This image contains over half a million galaxies and fifty thousand stars. Astronomers have studied this specific sky region for over two decades. The observatory's new camera provides unparalleled depth and coverage of the universe. Future observations will reveal even fainter galaxies and cosmic events.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: J&K: Days after Kulgam terror attack, man with grenade held in Pulwama
item.description: A suspect was apprehended in Pulwama carrying a hand grenade and anti-national posters. This arrest occurred during a security operation following recent migrant worker killings. Authorities booked the local man under stringent anti-terror laws, including the UAPA. Security forces are increasing patrols and checkpoints across the valley. This intensified security aims to maintain peace and prevent further unlawful activities.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Withdraw cases, allow youngsters to continue studies: SC to states
item.description: The Supreme Court permitted governments to withdraw cases against student protesters. This move aims to allow students to pursue their studies without prosecution fears. However, cases against individuals with criminal records will not be dropped. The court will also establish guidelines for the use of graded force by police. Discussions on modalities for dropping cases against genuine students are ongoing.
item.dc:creator: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA

item.title: Opposition toughens stand, washout of session likely
item.description: Parliament's monsoon session faces potential washout amid opposition demands. Opposition insists on discussing Ram temple donations and police actions. Union ministers criticize opposition for boycotting legislative proceedings. Bills were passed without debate due to the ongoing parliamentary standoff. The government has not yet assured discussions on the opposition's key demands.
item.dc:creator: KUMAR RAKESH AND SUBODH GHILDIYAL

item.title: Jeff Bezos warns Mamdani on NYC taxes, slams wasteful spending
item.description: Jeff Bezos commented on New York City's proposed pied-à-terre tax, calling it a fine thing for the city. He cautioned against aggressive tax increases, which could deter tourism and economic competitiveness. Bezos rejected targeting individuals like Ken Griffin, calling it a villain strategy. He argued that government spending inefficiencies are a greater concern than taxation levels. Bezos previously criticized New York City's public school spending and economic policies.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: 'Flavouring neutral alcohol isn't right in spirit'
item.description: The FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits. This practice misrepresents the true nature of alcoholic beverages and misleads consumers. Manufacturers were found using neutral alcohol and adding identical flavouring substances. Several companies, including United Spirits, faced prohibitions and notices. The regulator stressed that characteristic taste should develop naturally through base ingredients.
item.dc:creator: ANUJA JAISWAL

item.title: Humpback sightings fall 60% as weakened seabirds reach Australia’s east
item.description: Unusual whale and seabird sightings in the Southern Ocean suggest changing ocean conditions. Marine heat waves are affecting waters around Australia and Antarctica. These warming events disrupt food webs and push marine life off course. Limited monitoring hinders understanding of these significant ecosystem shifts. Better long-term data is urgently needed to track these accelerating changes.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Scientists survey Mount Ararat glacier above 5,000m for first ice core
item.description: A German-Turkish research team has completed the first scientific survey of the glacier on Mount Ararat, Turkey's highest peak, to study its potential as a record of climate and human history. Scientists mapped the shrinking ice cap to identify the best site for drilling the mountain's first ice core, hoping it will reveal thousands of years of environmental and archaeological information before melting erases it.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Lauren Sanchez worked at waterpark; 40 years later, she takes luxurious ocean trips
item.description: Lauren Sanchez's career evolved from a teenage waterpark job to ocean conservation leadership. She recently explored the Galápagos Islands, highlighting shark importance. The Bezos Earth Fund supports significant marine conservation projects in the region. These initiatives protect vast ocean areas and numerous marine species. Sanchez's work now focuses on protecting vital ocean ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: ARAI's study on E20 fuel impact may be made public
item.description: Government agencies are considering releasing the ARAI study on E20 fuel's impact. This report, submitted in June 2024, studied E10-compatible vehicles. Fuel consumption increased slightly for two-wheelers and cars in the study. Mass emissions met regulatory requirements for all vehicles tested. The release aims to remove misconceptions among vehicle users about E20 fuel.

item.title: UPS has attracted just 4% of NPS subscribers: Government
item.description: The Unified Pension Scheme for central government employees has seen low adoption rates. Only a small percentage of National Pension Trust subscribers have opted for this new scheme. The government introduced UPS with assured pension benefits and gratuity provisions. However, the response has been tepid, prompting an extension of the migration deadline. No changes are currently being considered to replace the Unified Pension Scheme.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Here's how Michael Phelps built his $100 million fortune in 2026
item.description: Michael Phelps turned his legendary Olympic achievements into a multi-million dollar empire. By securing high-value endorsements from renowned brands post-retirement, he also channeled his success into impactful ventures. His establishment of a foundation showcases his commitment to youth education in swimming and healthy living. Additionally, Phelps's investment in the mental health platform shows his suppport for emotional wellness.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Josh Allen’s family stood by him through rejection, injuries and NFL success
item.description: The story of Josh Allen illustrates how unwavering support from family and relentless hard work paved his way to NFL greatness. Despite rejections and early criticism, he learned the value of consistency from his father's example. Overcoming injuries and playoff disappointments, Allen's journey reveals that the heart of success often beats stronger in the shadows, driven by family faith.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: How LeBron James turned childhood pain into a $41M education mission
item.description: LeBron James established a scholarship program for Akron students. This initiative helps approximately eleven hundred students attend college. The program stems from his own childhood struggles with financial instability. He never attended college himself, entering the NBA directly after high school. This mission provides a realistic chance for education beyond high school.

item.title: SC: How can transgender ID cards be rendered invalid?
item.description: The Supreme Court has sought the government's response regarding the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act. Concerns were raised that the new law might erase existing benefits for transgender individuals. Senior advocates reported that hormone treatment is being denied due to fear of prosecution. They also alleged the discontinuation of the national portal for transgenders. The court questioned the retrospective invalidation of previously issued transgender identity cards.

item.title: A seat for JSP's 'school bag': Why Kishor's Bankipur win is a warning for BJP, RJD
item.description: Prashant Kishor achieved a remarkable victory in the Bankipur byelection, effectively breaking the BJP's three-decade dominance on the assembly seat. This triumph represents Kishor's resurgence in politics following his party's prior electoral drubbing in the state. He leveraged this win to critique Bihar's chief minister and emphasize the need for development. The outcome comes as an embarrassment for the current government's leadership.

item.title: India-origin cricketer Reddy handed 8-year ban by ICC for corruption
item.description: USA cricketer Bodugum Akhilesh Reddy has been banned from all cricket for eight years after an ICC tribunal found him guilty of three Anti-Corruption Code breaches linked to the 2025 Abu Dhabi T10. He was found to have attempted match-fixing, encouraged a teammate to participate, and deleted evidence during the investigation. His ban is effective from November 21, 2025.

item.title: Charles Dickens' quote on kindness, patience and a gentle heart for everyday life
item.description: Charles Dickens powerfully captured human struggles and social injustices in his novels. His early life hardships profoundly shaped his worldview and writing style. Dickens gave voice to ordinary people, highlighting issues like child labor and poverty. His memorable characters and vivid storytelling continue to resonate with readers globally. The author's message of kindness and compassion remains highly relevant today.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana: How workers can avail Rs 1.6 lakh housing aid
item.description: In Gujarat, registered construction workers have the opportunity to benefit from financial support aimed at housing through the Shree Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana. To qualify, applicants must have been registered with the welfare board for a minimum of two years. Following the acquisition of an e-Nirman Card and house allotment, they can submit their applications. Those approved will receive ₹1.6 lakh to assist in home ownership.

item.description: Shares of the Seattle-headquartered e-commerce and cloud giant had surged 15% on Friday after the company reported its fastest cloud revenue growth in over four years and increased its forecast for annual capital expenditure.

item.title: Centre raises windfall tax on petrol, diesel and ATF exports from August 3
item.description: India has increased export duties on petrol, diesel, and aviation fuel. These revised rates will be effective from August 3 for the next fortnight. Domestic fuel duties remain unchanged, providing stability for local consumers. This move follows a reduction in commercial LPG prices earlier this month. The government is assessing global conflicts' impact on India's supply chains.

item.title: India to build over 1,000 affordable homes in Seychelles
item.description: India will construct over one thousand affordable housing units in Seychelles. This project addresses the island nation's housing shortage and strengthens bilateral cooperation. The first phase of this development is scheduled for completion by the year 2029. India's National Buildings Construction Corporation will manage the entire project's planning and implementation. This initiative is part of a larger economic package and development partnership between the two nations.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Ramanand Sagar's son says Ranbir Kapoor has 'too much baggage' to play Lord Ram
item.description: Shiv Sagar, grandson of Ramanand Sagar, recently commented on the casting for the upcoming Ramayana film. He particularly lauded Yash as Ravan and Sai Pallavi as Sita, highlighting their deep cultural connection. However, Shiv Sagar voiced concerns about Ranbir Kapoor's ability to embody Lord Ram, citing his previous roles. Interestingly, Ranbir himself has expressed uncertainty about fitting this revered character during promotional events.

item.title: BJP holds Manjalpur in Gujarat, but with a much smaller victory margin
item.description: In a recent bypoll, the BJP claimed victory in the Manjalpur seat of Vadodara, Gujarat, with candidate Satish Patel triumphing over Congress's Bhikhabhai Rabari by a notable, though diminished, margin compared to past assembly election results. This election followed the passing of BJP MLA Yogesh Patel, highlighting a need for the party to reassess its strategies given the reduced lead in votes.

item.title: After Arjuna Awardee calls out Indian calendar, AICF moves to find solution
item.description: The All India Chess Federation (AICF) is working to hold the senior National Chess Championship in November-December 2026 after it was initially scheduled for March 2027. Following concerns raised by Grandmaster Abhijeet Gupta, the federation is in talks with stakeholders to finalise dates. AICF said a packed domestic and international calendar had forced the initial postponement.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER
